title: `VAR_*` and `STDDEV_*` of doubles: Welford, Chan merge
verdict: Welford; Chan merge with fma; no clamp
description: Welford's online update: `mean_differential = (x - mean) / count`, `new_mean = mean + mean_differential`, `dsquared += (x - new_mean) * (x - mean)`. Partial states merge by Chan et al.: `delta = s.mean - t.mean`, `mean = fma(n_s / n, delta, t.mean)`, `M2 = M2_s + M2_t + delta * delta * n_s * n_t / n`.

No values is NULL; the sample variance of one value is NULL; the population variance of one value is 0. No clamp and no finiteness check: 1.5.6 raised `OutOfRange` ("VARSAMP is out of range!") on non-finite values, 2.0 gives NaN (duckdb-nonfinite-aggregates).
The docs are silent on the algorithm and on one value: a docs gap.

Probed (`sverify_dev.probe_statistics`): of {4, 7, 13, 16} shifted by 0, 1e6, 1e8, 1e9 and 1e12, `VAR_SAMP` is 30 and `VAR_POP` 22.5 at every shift, as Welford's update keeps them; the textbook formula gives 29.33 at 1e8 and 0 at 1e9. Values whose textbook variance in doubles is negative give 0.0: Welford's terms `(x - new_mean) * (x - mean)` are products of two numbers of one sign, so the sum is never negative and no clamp is needed.
reference: D30 (#1022): `AggFn.var` is the exact moments rounded once, never below 0. DuckDB's Welford with Chan's merge is within the plan's bound of it (`stat_algo` `WELFORD_CHAN`, `Epsilon.statEps`, `FloatBounds.StdModel.core_var_chan`). A sample of one value is NULL in both.
